reasoning: Macro close-up of stem tissue showing white fluffy/cottony mycelial growth with numerous small black sclerotia embedded within, on bleached stem tissue. This is the classic diagnostic presentation of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum) — 'characteristic black sclerotia embedded within white fluffy mold on stem lesions.' The scattered black dots are sclerotia, not the linear pycnidia rows of Diaporthe or the microsclerotia pattern of Charcoal Rot.
